indigo-galaxy · exedev · 2026-11-25 01:21–01:37 UTC · Claude Code 2.1.331 · agents: claude-opus-5-5, effort xhigh · feat/stall @ 7caf0a9 · PR branch feat/report · one take, unedited

harness/report.py on a real run with two crashes: right numbers, but "time used" counts the outages

report.py ran on a live run of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents, once while the run was down and once after it finished. Every count on the page matches a count made with jq and sqlite3: 7 accepted merges, 0 rejected, 108 tool calls (lead 21, h1/h2/h3 29 each), board requests per agent, merges per agent, messages sent and received, and 2 resumes with their down times and two down bands on the timeline. The page loads nothing from the network, escapes markup from the records, and passes shoot.py at 1280 and 400 px in both themes. Three things are wrong. "time used 10m 29s of 45 min" counts 4 min 24 s of outage that the deadline gave back. Two legend swatches escape the legend to the page's top corners. And labels of merges close in time overlap.

Findings

  1. "time used" counts the time the run was down. used is DONE − started and is shown as "10m 29s of 45 min" (report.py:323). The deadline was moved 264.26 s for the two outages, so the budget it is compared with excludes them; the team ran 6 min 6 s. During the outage the same field read "4m 20s" while the timeline showed 2m 49s. Subtracting the sum of down_s from records/resumes.jsonl (and open pauses) would make it comparable. template/harness/report.py:262
  2. Two legend swatches leave the legend. The legend uses <i class="k act"> and <i class="k gone"> (report.py:242, 244). The lane rules .act{position:absolute;top:8px;…} (408) and .gone{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;right:0;…} (414) apply to them too. Nothing in the legend is positioned, so they land at the page's top edge (a blue square above the title) and its top-right corner. Chromium: .k.act at (464, 8), .k.gone at (1268, 0). template/harness/report.py:408
  3. Labels of merges close in time overlap. Each statement's label is placed at its merge time (.m.done, report.py:412) with no collision handling. Five merges within 55 s of an 11.5-minute window read "ro… bas p… intervals" at 1280 px; at 400 px only "intervals". The chips row and the merges table still name all seven. template/harness/report.py:208
  4. White text on green is low in contrast. Done chips and labels are #fff on --ok: 3.5:1 in the light theme (#1f9d55) and 2.0:1 in the dark theme (#3ccf7a); WCAG AA asks 4.5:1 for text this size (report.py:370, 373, 412). template/harness/report.py:390
  5. The resumes table prints raw fields. The detail column is the record's key=value list: deadline_before=1795572502.2455816, deadline_after=1795572690.0635717, removed=[], landed=['roman', …]. Epoch seconds are hard to read; "deadline +187.8 s" or clock times would say the same thing. template/harness/report.py:311

Not covered

  • Rejected merges, pauses, removals, blocked actions and a stall: none happened in this run, so those rows and marks were not exercised live (the stub tests cover them).
  • The report written before a launch ("not launched yet") on a fresh work directory: only on the scratch copy of the archive's records (regen-test/).
  • Browsers other than Chromium.

Audit trail

One take, lifecycle.cast; no take was discarded. It ran from 01:21:20 to 01:37:25 UTC. Every keystroke in it came from rec.sh type/run, sent by me (an agent); no person typed.

Expected values and tolerances were written to expected.md at 01:20 UTC, before the take; chapter 1 shows its timestamp. The pre-kill values for each crash were written by crash.sh (snapshot prekill-N) before the kill.

Crash 1 was not as tight as planned. watch-team.sh fired at 01:25:21 when 2 statements had landed, but crash.sh's first snapshot took 51 s: my procs.sh forked twice per /proc entry (931 processes, about 40 s a scan). Meanwhile four more statements landed, and the kill came at 01:26:12 with 6 of 7 on main. So prekill-1 is not the state right before kill 1. The state at the kill is down-1, read after every writer was dead (no process of the run left, gateway SIGKILLed; the gateway log's last record is 01:26:11.217, before the kill). Before crash 2 I replaced it with a one-pass procs.py; prekill-2 was written 1.3 s before kill 2. The line "processes under run/ after 1s: none" in crash 1 means "at the first scan", which itself took about 30 s.

harness/boss.sh trust was run right after the launch and after each resume, as SKILL.md says. After the launch it answered yes in lead, h1, h2 and h3; after both resumes it reported "started without a prompt" for all four (the folders were already trusted). No other prompt was answered for the user. I sent nothing to the agents: no boss.sh say, no keys into their windows. The seven team msg messages were the agents' own.

The take's shell was started with my session's CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_* and ANTHROPIC_* variables removed (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR kept), so selftest.sh's claude -p ran as a plain session. The team's tmux session takes its environment from the default tmux server. Its windows were 188×66 (the server's window-size latest).

The brief points to a section "Things to know before demoing the live team" in proof/README.md; that section does not exist (the README ends with shoot.py). I followed "Watching another tmux session" and read the team only with tmux capture-pane -p.

Outside the take: one read-only sqlite3 -readonly look at the board at 01:25:34 and jq reads of records/gateway.jsonl while the run went on; the screenshots (shoot.py, bin/frames.py, which seeks the same asciinema-player as this page); bin/readback.sh; two scratch report runs (escape-test/, regen-test/) on copies of the archived records.

Clean-up: ./teardown.sh --archive stopped the session and the gateway at 01:36:37. At 01:37:20 tmux ls listed no demo-lifecycle session and procs.py found no process of the run. The two scratch copies (fresh/, stopped-copy/) were purged and deleted inside the take. Nothing I started is still running. Left on disk under /home/exedev/codes/tat-dev/demo/lifecycle: run/ (template files, report.html, harness/__pycache__), archive-out/, unpack/, clone/, venv/, evidence/, frames/, shots/, pages-src/.

Redactions: none were needed. A grep of the cast and of the pages for API keys, tokens, ~/.claude and ~/.ssh paths and e-mail addresses found nothing.
